Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

contentiousR (development version)

New data

  • conflict_data() and add_conflict() gain dataset = "raqed": the Revolutionary and Quasi-revolutionary Episodes Dataset (RAQED) v1.4, 2000-2026, HSE University. RAQED is the renamed successor of the CSRA Revolutionary Database. Columns use the raqed_ prefix, and raqed_type_re, raqed_type_re_q, and raqed_type_qre are dummies for the source’s episode type.
  • conflict_data() and add_conflict() gain dataset = "omg": the Opposition Movements and Groups (OMG) dataset v1, 1789-2019 (Dahl et al. 2026), at the campaign-phase level. omg_onset marks a campaign’s first phase and omg_phase_onset every phase.
  • conflict_data() and add_conflict() gain dataset = "arc": the Anatomy of Resistance Campaigns (ARC) 2.0 events, 1990-2018 (Vüllers et al. 2026), aggregated to country-year: event counts by source and by maximalist demands, and the number of events with, and distinct organizations taking part in, dissent.
  • conflict_data() and add_conflict() gain dataset = "navco3.0": the NAVCO 3.0 event data on 26 countries, 1990-2012 (Chenoweth, Pinckney, and Lewis 2018), aggregated to counts of campaign actions by tactic and goal, state concessions and repression, and fatality, injury, and participant ranges.
  • cn_cite("raqed"), cn_cite("omg"), cn_cite("arc"), and cn_cite("navco3.0") return the new citations.

Country-quarter, country-month, and country-day panels

  • build_states_panel() gains unit = c("year", "quarter", "month", "day"). Quarterly panels add a quarter column, monthly panels a month column, daily panels month, day, and date. Yearly panels are unchanged.
  • conflict_data() gains unit, and add_conflict() detects the panel’s unit: event data are aggregated, and campaign and episode records placed, by the month or day of their start date. SCAD, MM, MMAD, ARC, NAVCO 3.0, Beissinger, RAQED, MEC, and OMG support all units; NAVCO 1.3, NAVCO 2.1, UCDP/PRIO, and UCDP VPP record only years and error for a finer unit. Records dated less precisely than the unit are dropped with a message.
  • add_lag() and add_spell_duration() count months or days in sub-annual panels. plot_coverage() shows them by year. as_peacesciencer_panel(), add_from_peacesciencer(), and harmonize_conflict_data() require a country-year panel.
  • conflict_data(dataset = "beissinger") gains beissinger_startdatetxt, the source’s start date text.
  • load_leader_data() gains unit, and add_leader_data() detects the panel’s unit. Leaders are placed by their dates in office, so each period gets the leader in power at its end (Mubarak in January 2011, Tantawi from February). Finer units add leader_tenure_quarters, leader_tenure_months, or leader_tenure_days; leader_tenure still counts calendar years. REIGN supports up to months.
  • New aggregate_panel() collapses a country-day, country-month, or country-quarter panel to a coarser unit: counts are summed, indicators and maxima take the maximum, other columns take the value of the last period, and lags and spell counters are dropped. The rules can be overridden per column.

Coverage, zero-filling, and episodes in progress

  • add_conflict() gains fill_zero = FALSE. With fill_zero = TRUE, event indicators and counts are 0 in periods the dataset covers but records nothing, and stay NA outside its coverage. Coverage is defined per dataset: global datasets cover every state, SCAD, ARC, and NAVCO 3.0 the countries they record, MM the country-years it lists, and MMAD each country from its first to its last recorded year.
  • add_conflict() adds <prefix>incidence and <prefix>n_active for NAVCO 1.3, NAVCO 2.1, Beissinger, RAQED, MEC, and OMG: whether, and how many, episodes were in progress in each period, from start to end date. Onset columns are unchanged.
  • conflict_data(dataset = "navco1.3") gains nvc1.3_EYEAR, the campaign’s end year.
  • New list_datasets() lists the bundled datasets with their years, countries, record type, supported units, column prefix, and coverage rule.

Bug fixes

Country codes

Several states were silently dropped or matched to the wrong country, because countrycode converts codes without regard to the year and has no equivalent for some states. Conversions between COW and Gleditsch-Ward codes now go through one year-aware function, used by every loader.

  • GW panels from build_states_panel(coding_system = "gw") had no Vietnam (GW 816) and, with exclude_microstates = FALSE, no Caribbean island states or other microstates: rows were dropped when countrycode had no country name for the code. Names now fall back to the states package. Abkhazia and South Ossetia are now removed by exclude_non_un = TRUE.
  • COW panels code West Germany as 255 and Czechoslovakia as 316, but data using standard COW codes (NMC population and military expenditure, V-Dem, Archigos and REIGN leaders, SIPRI, and the conflict datasets) kept 260 and 315, so West Germany (1955-1989) and Czechoslovakia (up to 1992) got no data in COW panels, including NAVCO, MEC, and OMG campaigns such as the Prague Spring. All loaders now use the panels’ codes. as_peacesciencer_panel() and add_from_peacesciencer() give peacesciencer the standard COW codes (ccode 260 and 315).
  • Yemen: GW-coded sources (UCDP/PRIO, UCDP VPP, Fariss, Barnum) were not matched to COW 679 (Yemen from 1990), e.g. 19 conflict-years of UCDP/PRIO; COW-coded sources lost Yemen from 1990 in GW panels. Sources that code Yemen as one unit throughout now give COW 678 up to 1990.
  • Serbia: GW panels code Yugoslavia as 345 up to 2006 and Serbia as 340 after, but conversions used one code for all years, so Serbia’s data were lost in one period or the other (e.g. Gapminder, SIPRI, NMC, V-Dem, MEC, MMAD, RAQED). Germany before 1945 (GW 255) and Vietnam were lost in COW panels with GW-coded sources (Fariss, Barnum).
  • Mass Mobilization uses its own codes for several states. Kosovo (MM 341) was matched to Montenegro (COW 341), and Yugoslavia and Serbia and Montenegro (1992-2006), Serbia and Montenegro from 2006, the USSR, South Sudan, Ethiopia from 2016, and Yemen from 2016 were not matched at all.
  • add_regions() returned NA for Serbia, and in GW panels for Yemen, Czechoslovakia, and Vietnam.
  • harmonize_conflict_data() converts country names by year too (Serbia in COW panels and Yemen in GW panels were dropped), and with aggregate = FALSE no longer errors when year_col is "year" or country_col is the panel’s code column.

UN World Population Prospects

  • The WPP population data are rebuilt reproducibly from the ‘wpp2024’ package (data-raw/extdata.R). The previous extract had been matched to COW codes by country name, which left out Serbia and Yugoslavia entirely, and gave historical states the population of today’s country with the same code: e.g. the USSR had Russia’s population (139 instead of 267 million in 1980), Pakistan before 1971 lacked East Pakistan, and West Germany had the population of unified Germany.
  • load_population_data(dataset = "wpp") now assigns each WPP country to the state that governed it in each year: states that later split are the sum of their parts (USSR, Yugoslavia, Czechoslovakia, Ethiopia, Pakistan, Sudan, Indonesia with Timor-Leste, Malaysia with Singapore, the United Arab Republic), Hong Kong and Macao join China from 1997 and 1999, and parts of later unified states that WPP cannot separate are NA (the two Germanys and Yemens before 1990, the two Vietnams before 1976, Tanganyika and Zanzibar before 1964). It returns only the years each state exists, and works the same way for GW codes.

Other bug fixes

  • plot_temporal_coverage() skipped periods without events instead of plotting 0, so lines ran straight across gaps.
  • cn_cite("gapminder") and cn_cite("vdem") now return citations, like every other dataset = value.
  • Documentation: Barnum et al. coverage is 1816-2023 (military burden to 2019); the Gapminder file runs to 2100, and its most recent years are forecasts and projections, not observations.
  • load_leader_data(dataset = "reign") dropped leaders still in office when the REIGN data end (no exit date in the source), so every country-year of their tenure was missing (e.g. Russia from 2000 on): 135 of 194 countries had a leader in 2015 and 29 in 2021, against 194 now. They are now kept in office through August 2021, the last month REIGN covers. When two leaders took office in the same month, the later one by day is now kept, as the year-end leader.
  • In a country-month or country-day panel, add_conflict() with an episode dataset (Beissinger, RAQED, MEC, OMG) added a day column, which made the panel look like a country-day panel to later functions.
  • conflict_data(dataset = "mm") counted the source’s protest = 0 rows, which mark country-years without a protest, as protests: 1,906 of 4,877 country-years had mm_onset = 1 and mm_n_protests = 1 but no protest. They now have mm_onset = 0 and mm_n_protests = 0.

Package size

  • The SIPRI military expenditure data are now stored as a compact .rds table built from the two workbook sheets the package uses, instead of the full ten-sheet .xlsx workbook (0.9 MB to 0.12 MB). load_military_expenditure_data(dataset = "sipri") returns exactly the same data as before and no longer reads the workbook with ‘readxl’.

Breaking changes

  • dataset = "csra" is removed: the CSRA Revolutionary Database has been renamed RAQED. conflict_data() and add_conflict() now stop with a message pointing to dataset = "raqed" (version 1.4), and the CSRA v1.102 file is no longer bundled.

contentiousR 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-15

Changes made for CRAN

  • The package title is now “Contentious Politics and Civil Conflict Research”.
  • cn_cite() now returns its result visibly instead of printing it with cat(). The result is a bibentry object with the additional class cn_citation; typing cn_cite("archigos") at the console still shows the BibTeX, and print() shows it explicitly.
  • The bundled data files are smaller (tarball 4.3 MB): they keep only the columns the package reads, and the MEC and NMC Stata files are stored as compressed .rds. Loader output is unchanged. ‘haven’ is no longer used.
  • citation("contentiousR") now lists the SSRN preprint describing the package, followed by the software citation.

Bug fixes

  • load_vdem_data(coding_system = "cow") no longer silently drops East Germany (COW 265, 1949-1990); it was previously excluded only in the "cow" branch, so V-Dem coverage for Germany differed depending on the chosen coding system with no indication why.
  • add_spell_duration() now computes spells from the actual calendar-year difference instead of row position within a state. A gap in the input years (e.g. left by tidyr::drop_na(event), which the package’s own examples recommend) previously understated the elapsed time.
  • plot_coverage() now errors with a clear message instead of crashing when drop_empty = TRUE removes every state (e.g. the chosen event never occurs in the supplied panel/year range).
  • cn_cite() matched keywords by substring, so a short dataset name (e.g. "mm") could also match an unrelated entry whose keyword merely contained it as a substring ("mmad"). Keyword matching is now exact against the comma-separated keyword list.
  • harmonize_conflict_data(): a factor year_col was coerced with as.integer(), which returns the factor’s internal level codes rather than the printed year. It is now converted to character first. A date_col that fails to parse (e.g. a non-ISO format without a matching date_format) now raises a clear error instead of a generic base-R one.

Bring your own data

  • Added harmonize_conflict_data() to join externally supplied conflict/ event data (GDELT, ICEWS, ACLED, or anything else not bundled with contentiousR) onto a state panel: it maps the caller’s country column to COW/GW codes via countrycode::countrycode(), extracts a year from either a pre-parsed year_col or a date_col/date_format, optionally aggregates event-level rows to country-year (<prefix>_onset, <prefix>_n_events), and joins the result in. Unlike add_conflict(), it never downloads or bundles data itself, so contentiousR gains no dependency on gdeltr2, icews, or acled.api.

Visualization

  • plot_coverage() gained a show_labels argument (default TRUE). Set it to FALSE to drop the per-row country/code labels, which otherwise overlap and become illegible once the panel covers more than a few dozen states.
  • plot_regional_coverage()’s region labels are now horizontal and word-wrapped instead of angled, and its region field’s canonical “Middle East” label is the shorter “Middle East & North Africa” form. plot_temporal_coverage()’s period labels are now vertical instead of angled. Both plots no longer set a ggplot2 title (redundant with a caption in a manuscript).
  • Added plot_regional_coverage() and plot_temporal_coverage() to compare regional and temporal event coverage across any combination of conflict_data() campaign/episode datasets, plus a “Comparing revolutionary-event datasets” article reproducing the descriptive exercise in Guseinov, Ustyuzhanin & Korotayev (2026).
  • Added add_regions() to join one or more countrycode region classifications (region, region23, un.region.name, un.regionsub.name) onto a state panel by cow/gw code.

Data

  • Added the Major Episodes of Contention (MEC) dataset: 2,734 globally covered reformist and maximalist episodes from 1955 through 2018. MEC is available through conflict_data(dataset = "mec") and add_conflict(dataset = "mec"). Episode-level rows are preserved unless the existing aggregate = TRUE policy is requested.

Correctness

  • fetch_campaign_events() (used by plot_regional_coverage() and plot_temporal_coverage()) now compares NAVCO 2.1 at the same campaign-onset level as the other datasets, using conflict_data()’s own nvc2.1_ONSET flag (keyed on the numeric campaign id) instead of re-deriving onsets from the campaign name, which is not unique and could silently merge distinct campaigns that happen to share a name.
  • fetch_campaign_events()’s region field now stays at exactly 7 categories. countrycode::countrycode()’s "region" destination labels a few pre-1990 historical entities (Yemen Arab Republic, Yemen People’s Republic, the United Arab Republic) with the World Bank’s older “Middle East & North Africa” string while every other MENA country gets the newer “Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan & Pakistan” string; since campaign data covering the 1950s-80s includes those historical codes, the region was silently splitting into two bars in plot_regional_coverage()/plot_temporal_coverage().
  • gdp_growth (load_gdp_data(), dataset = "gapminder") is now NA unless the preceding row is genuinely one year earlier for the same country, the same gap-safety check add_lag() uses.
  • Removed add_pop(). It was an exact duplicate of add_population() (same body, same arguments, two visually identical Reference entries) and every other add_*()/load_*_data() pair in the package already shares one name (add_vdem()/load_vdem_data(), add_leader_data()/load_leader_data(), etc.) – add_population() is the one that matches load_population_data(). Use add_population() instead.
  • Renamed add_spells() to add_spell_duration() to stop it silently shadowing (or being shadowed by) peacesciencer::add_spells() when both packages are attached in the same session – the two are similar in spirit but not interchangeable (contentiousR’s version works on any binary _onset/_incidence/_ongoing column, not a fixed set of bundled columns).
  • conflict_data() now applies start_year and end_year consistently to every bundled source.
  • UCDP/PRIO output now distinguishes conflict incidence from episode onset. ucdp_prio_onset is based on start_date2; the new ucdp_prio_incidence column identifies all active conflict-years.
  • SCAD country-year totals now exclude UCDP placeholder records, deduplicate multi-location rows by event ID, and treat documented negative death-count codes as missing.
  • All-missing groups now produce NA instead of -Inf, NaN, and associated warnings during conflict aggregation.
  • Mass Mobilization participant strings are retained in mm_participants_reported; mm_participants summarizes only exact numeric reports.
  • add_conflict() no longer re-aggregates sources that are already unique by country-year, preventing character-valued source fields from being dropped.

API and robustness

  • Added as_peacesciencer_panel() to supply the state-year key aliases and metadata required by peacesciencer while preserving contentiousR’s API.
  • Added add_from_peacesciencer() to apply a state-year peacesciencer function while keeping temporary ccode/gwcode keys out of the result.
  • build_states_cow_panel() is internal again (not exported). It’s the actual COW-panel implementation build_states_panel(coding_system = "cow") dispatches to, but there’s no public reason to call it directly instead of build_states_panel() – and its GW counterpart, build_states_gw_panel(), was never exported in the first place.
  • Added strict validation for years, logical flags, panel keys, and output-key uniqueness.
  • build_states_panel() now validates start_year/end_year against the Correlates of War / Gleditsch-Ward state system’s actual coverage: 1816-2025.
  • Added ucdp_vpp_incidence. The existing ucdp_vpp_onset column remains as a compatibility alias and is now documented as incidence rather than onset.
  • Removed the magrittr dependency in favor of R’s native pipe.

Release infrastructure

  • Added broader test coverage, two introductory vignettes, package-level documentation, data provenance and licensing notes, pkgdown configuration, and GitHub Actions for package checks and site deployment.
  • Added a case study article assembling a panel and modeling revolutionary onset, and a “Comparing revolutionary-event datasets” article (see Visualization above).
  • Added a package logo, shown in the README and the pkgdown site navbar.
  • Added formal References sections to load_gdp_data()/add_gdp(), load_population_data()/add_population(), load_military_expenditure_data()/add_military_expenditure(), load_vdem_data()/add_vdem(), conflict_data()/add_conflict(), load_leader_data()/add_leader_data(), and plot_regional_coverage()/plot_temporal_coverage(), citing the underlying data source(s) for each.
  • Corrected the SCAD citation’s DOI (in DESCRIPTION and the bundled bibliography behind cn_cite()): the previous DOI did not resolve.
